title: Reconcile hook timeout defaults: RLM_TIMEOUT 60s exceeds documented 30s hook timeout
description:
The hook's internal timeout default is 60s (CONFIG.timeout, RLM_TIMEOUT, rlm-hook.mjs ~line 37; also documented in README.md Configuration), but both README.md (Installation section settings.json snippet) and install.sh (printed settings snippet) tell users to register the hook with "timeout": 30. Claude Code will kill the hook at 30s, before the hook's own 60s SIGTERM/SIGKILL handling (invokeHaiku, ~line 876) ever fires — so on slow agentic runs the graceful-degradation path (exit 0, no output) is bypassed by an external kill.

Fix (pick one and make all three places consistent):
a) raise the snippet timeout in README.md and install.sh to a value above RLM_TIMEOUT (e.g. 90), or
b) lower the RLM_TIMEOUT default below the snippet's 30s (e.g. 25000ms), or
c) document explicitly that RLM_TIMEOUT must be set below the hooks timeout and choose coherent defaults.

Acceptance criteria:
- README.md snippet, install.sh snippet, and CONFIG.timeout default are mutually coherent (internal timeout strictly less than registered hook timeout)
- README Latency profile / Configuration sections reflect the chosen values
- No test regressions: node --test test/unit.test.mjs green

title: Add dollar-cost estimates to the metrics dashboard
description:
plan.md Open Questions item 6 (Cost tracking): "Each agentic run consumes
Haiku tokens... Need to measure actual usage" -- still listed unresolved
even though Phase 5's metrics pipeline already captures token_estimate
per event (bench/parse-log.mjs aggregate(), rlm-hook.mjs recordMetric()).
The dashboard (bench/dashboard.mjs, README "Phase 5: Metrics dashboard")
currently shows latency distribution, cache-hit rate, and per-mode counts,
but never turns token_estimate into an actual cost figure -- so the
"Need to measure actual usage" question is answerable from data the tool
already logs, just not surfaced.

Add a per-day and overall estimated-cost column to the dashboard, computed
from token_estimate (input/output token counts) x the current Haiku
pricing (make the per-token rates a constant near the top of
bench/parse-log.mjs or bench/dashboard.mjs so they're easy to update when
pricing changes -- do not hardcode inline in the render loop).

Acceptance criteria:
- aggregate() in bench/parse-log.mjs adds an estimated_cost_usd figure
  per day and overall, from existing token_estimate data (null/absent
  when no token_estimate present in a day's records, matching the
  existing null-handling convention for latency percentiles)
- renderHTML() in bench/dashboard.mjs displays it in the summary cards
  and per-day table
- Add test coverage alongside the existing Group 25/26 tests in
  test/unit.test.mjs
- plan.md Open Questions item 6 updated to note the fix

title: Capture Haiku token/usage counts in metrics (prerequisite for cost tracking / bf-1pp)
description:
GAP: plan.md Phase 5 goal (line 145) lists "model cost" as an objective and Phase 5 is marked COMPLETE, but no token/usage data is captured anywhere. recordMetric() in rlm-hook.mjs only stamps latency_ms, mode, input_len, cache_hit, and text extras (reason/source/intent) -- there is no token field. The SDK paths callMessagesSDK() and callHaikuAgenticSDK() in rlm-hook.mjs receive an Anthropic response object that carries response.usage (input_tokens/output_tokens) but discard it: both return only extractSDKText(response). The subprocess path invokeHaiku() spawns claude with --output-format text, which returns no usage at all. grep for 'token_estimate' across rlm-hook.mjs, bench/, and test/ returns nothing.

Consequence: bf-1pp ("Add dollar-cost estimates to the metrics dashboard") is written on the false premise that "Phase 5's metrics pipeline already captures token_estimate per event" -- it does not, so bf-1pp cannot be completed as written; there is no token data to turn into a cost figure. This bead is the missing upstream prerequisite. plan.md Open Question 6 (Cost tracking: "Need to measure actual usage") remains genuinely unaddressed.

Scope / approach:
- SDK path: read response.usage from callMessagesSDK() and callHaikuAgenticSDK() (sum input_tokens/output_tokens across agentic turns) and thread it up to the main() 'complete' exit so recordMetric() can stamp a token field (e.g. input_tokens/output_tokens or a token_estimate).
- Subprocess path: usage is not available under --output-format text. Either switch that spawn to --output-format json and read usage from the envelope, or record a rough estimate from input_len + output length so the field is populated consistently across both paths. Whichever is chosen, keep the metrics-write bullet-proof (a usage-capture failure must never change exit behavior, matching appendMetric's existing swallow-all contract).

Acceptance criteria:
- recordMetric('complete', ...) (and, where meaningful, cache/skip exits) records a token count field for both the SDK and subprocess Haiku paths.
- bench/parse-log.mjs aggregate() surfaces the per-day/overall token totals (or the field is at least present for bf-1pp's cost math to consume), with the same null-when-absent convention as latency percentiles.
- Unit test coverage alongside Groups 24/25 for the new field (inline faithful-copy style, matching the existing metrics tests).
- plan.md Open Question 6 updated to reference the fix; note bf-1pp depends on this.

title: Scope agentic-mode Bash(rm:*) permission to the scratch file only
description:
invokeHaiku() (rlm-hook.mjs) grants agentic-mode Haiku
--allowedTools 'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Bash(git:*),Bash(rm:*)'. The
Bash(rm:*) entry is unscoped -- it permits any `rm` invocation Claude
Code's own tool-permission matcher accepts for the `rm` command, not just
cleanup of the scratch file the hook itself creates
(.claude/rlm-scratch.md, see docs/notes/architecture.md "Agentic mode").
The stated purpose (per architecture.md: "Haiku writes scratch notes to
.claude/rlm-scratch.md as it explores, then deletes the file") only needs
permission to remove that one path.

Narrow the allowed pattern to the specific scratch file, e.g.
`Bash(rm .claude/rlm-scratch.md)` (or the SDK-mode equivalent scoping
already used by isAllowedGitCommand()/toolBashGit() for git -- note the
SDK tool-loop path in dispatchAgenticTool() already restricts Bash to
git-only via isAllowedGitCommand(), so this gap is specific to the CLI
subprocess path's --allowedTools flag, not the SDK path).

Acceptance criteria:
- --allowedTools no longer grants unscoped rm
- Existing integration test coverage for scratch-file cleanup
  (test/integration.test.mjs) still passes
- docs/notes/architecture.md's "Agentic mode" bullet on tool scope
  updated to reflect the narrower permission

title: Make SHA-256 cache writes atomic (tmp+rename)
description:
plan.md Open Questions item 7 (Race conditions): "If the user submits two
prompts rapidly, two hook invocations run concurrently. Cache writes are
not atomic -- last writer wins. Acceptable for now; use a lock file in
Phase 3+ if needed." Phase 3-5 shipped without addressing this; saveCache()
in rlm-hook.mjs still writes the JSON cache file directly.

The semantic-cache index (updateCacheIndex(), rlm-hook.mjs) already uses a
tmp-file + rename pattern -- reuse that same approach for saveCache()
instead of introducing a separate lock file, which is simpler and avoids
partial/corrupt cache file reads on concurrent writes (a corrupt cache
file currently degrades gracefully via checkCache()'s parse-failure path,
but still wastes the write and forces a re-run on the next lookup).

Acceptance criteria:
- saveCache() writes to a temp path under RLM_CACHE_DIR then renames into
  place (same pattern as updateCacheIndex)
- Add a unit test asserting no partial/truncated file is ever visible at
  the final cache path even if the write is interrupted mid-way (can
  simulate via an injectable writeFile that throws after a partial write,
  matching the existing test style for other cache helpers)
- plan.md Open Questions item 7 updated to note the fix

title: Skip CLAUDE.md/plugin/hook discovery in Haiku subprocess spawn
description:
invokeHaiku() in rlm-hook.mjs spawns the claude CLI with only -p, --model,
--output-format, --add-dir, --permission-mode, and (agentic mode)
--allowedTools/--max-turns. It does not pass --safe-mode, so the
preresearch subprocess pays for CLAUDE.md auto-discovery, skills, plugins,
custom commands/agents, and (per `claude --help`) the user's own
UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hooks -- none of which are needed for a
throwaway -p preresearch call, and the hooks case is a real correctness
risk (this hook's own subprocess could re-trigger other configured hooks,
e.g. anything wired to UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse in the invoking user's
settings.json).

Add --safe-mode to the args array built in invokeHaiku() (rlm-hook.mjs,
around the `const args = [...]` block before spawn('claude', args, ...)).
Do NOT use --bare instead -- its help text states it forces
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/apiKeyHelper auth and never reads OAuth/keychain, which
would break the subprocess path's whole reason for existing (see
docs/notes/architecture.md "Why subprocess instead of SDK": ride the
user's Max subscription, no separate API key). --safe-mode explicitly
keeps "Auth, model selection, built-in tools, and permissions" working
normally while dropping CLAUDE.md/skills/plugins/hooks/etc.

Acceptance criteria:
- invokeHaiku() passes --safe-mode in both agentic and fast/detailed
  invocation paths
- Existing unit/integration tests (test/unit.test.mjs,
  test/integration.test.mjs) still pass
- Manually verify (or add a test double for) a measurable startup-latency
  delta before/after on a repo with a nontrivial CLAUDE.md

title: Add --stats CLI flag for instant terminal metrics summary
description:
The only way to see hook performance today is running the HTTP dashboard
(node bench/dashboard.mjs --serve, README "Phase 5: Metrics dashboard"),
which requires starting and later stopping a local server just to check
skip rate / cache-hit rate / p50-p95 latency -- high friction for a tool
that's meant to be a quick, low-ceremony local CLI utility.

Add a `rlm-hook.mjs --stats` flag (alongside the existing `--version`
flag mentioned in docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1 deliverables) that reads
RLM_METRICS_FILE, runs the existing aggregate() logic from
bench/parse-log.mjs (import/reuse it, don't duplicate the aggregation
math), and prints a compact plain-text summary to stdout: total events,
skip rate + top skip reasons, cache-hit rate, p50/p95 latency, and
per-mode breakdown for the overall period. No HTTP server, no file
output -- just a terminal-friendly digest of what the dashboard already
computes.

Acceptance criteria:
- `node rlm-hook.mjs --stats` (or the installed `rlm-hook --stats`)
  prints a readable summary and exits 0 without needing --serve
- Reuses aggregate()/read-log logic from bench/parse-log.mjs rather than
  reimplementing it
- Add a unit test covering the flag's output shape (can reuse
  bench/fixtures if present)
- README "Phase 5: Metrics dashboard" section documents the flag as a
  lighter-weight alternative to the dashboard server

title: Cache key doesn't include cwd -- cross-project cache collisions
description:
getCacheKey(input) in rlm-hook.mjs hashes only the prompt text (per
docs/notes/architecture.md "Cache Design": "Key: SHA-256 of the raw user
message... keyed on message text only, not on cwd or model"). This is
called out as an accepted tradeoff in the notes, but plan.md's Open
Questions item 5 ("Multi-project sessions... cache should be invalidated
or keyed differently") is still listed unresolved -- and the actual
failure mode is worse than "shared cache is fine": in agentic mode the
cached JSON includes relevant_files with paths and per-file purposes
(see README "Example output"), which are only meaningful relative to the
project they were generated in. The same short prompt ("add retry logic")
issued in two different repos will return the first repo's file paths
inside the second repo's <rlm_preresearch> block, actively misleading the
main model instead of just wasting a cache slot.

Fix: incorporate a hash of cwd into getCacheKey() (e.g.
sha256(prompt + '\n' + cwd)), so cache entries are project-scoped.
Update saveCache/checkCache call sites (already keyed via getCacheKey())
-- no other changes needed. Applies to both the SHA-256 exact-match cache
and the semantic (embedding) cache's key scheme.

Acceptance criteria:
- getCacheKey(prompt, cwd) is project-scoped; same prompt in two
  different cwd values produces different keys
- Existing cache unit tests updated/extended to cover the cwd dimension
- plan.md Open Questions item 5 updated to reference the fix

title: Implement --session-id/--resume wiring for warm Haiku sessions (ADR-001)
description:
First implementation slice of docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (Resume warm
per-conversation Haiku sessions instead of cold subprocess spawns).

Add:
- CONFIG.sessionResume, env var RLM_SESSION_RESUME (default false)
- A helper that derives a stable session UUID from the hook's
  transcript_path input (sha256 -> uuid-formatted string)
- In invokeHaiku() (rlm-hook.mjs), when CONFIG.sessionResume is true:
  first cache-miss turn of a conversation passes --session-id <id>;
  subsequent cache-miss turns pass --resume <id> instead of a bare
  spawn. Needs a small on-disk marker (e.g. under RLM_CACHE_DIR,
  keyed by the derived session id) to know "have we started this
  session before" across separate hook process invocations.
- Fallback: any --resume failure (nonzero exit mentioning missing/
  invalid session, or timeout) retries once as a fresh non-resumed
  spawn, consistent with the hook's existing exit-0-on-any-error
  contract -- never block the conversation.
- A turn cap (e.g. RLM_SESSION_RESUME_MAX_TURNS, default ~20) after
  which the next turn starts a fresh session instead of resuming,
  to bound Haiku history growth per ADR-001's Consequences section.

Gate behind RLM_SESSION_RESUME=true (default off) until latency/cost
is validated per ADR-001. Reference: docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for session-id derivation (deterministic per
  transcript_path, distinct across paths) and the resume/fallback
  branch logic (can inject a fake spawn like the existing
  invokeHaiku tests do)
- Feature is a no-op (identical behavior to today) when
  RLM_SESSION_RESUME is unset/false

title: Pid-scope the CLI agentic scratch file to prevent concurrent-run collisions
description:
Plan Open Question 2 (docs/plan/plan.md, Open Questions section) flags that the fixed scratch path .claude/rlm-scratch.md can collide. The SDK agentic path already resolved this with a pid-scoped file (sdkScratchPath in rlm-hook.mjs, ~line 1167: .claude/rlm-scratch-<pid>.md), but the SUBPROCESS agentic path did not: buildRLMPrompt (rlm-hook.mjs ~line 716) hardcodes scratchFile = '.claude/rlm-scratch.md' into the Haiku prompt, and main() (~line 1808) cleans up that same fixed path in a finally block. Two concurrent hook invocations (user submits prompts rapidly — plan Open Question 5) will overwrite each other's notes, and one run's cleanup can delete the other run's scratch mid-exploration.

Fix: use a pid-scoped scratch filename in buildRLMPrompt for the agentic subprocess prompt (mirror sdkScratchPath naming), and have main() clean up that same pid-scoped path. Keep the Bash(rm:*) allowedTools entry working for Haiku's self-cleanup step.

Acceptance criteria:
- buildRLMPrompt no longer embeds the fixed '.claude/rlm-scratch.md' path; the path includes process.pid (or equivalent unique token)
- main()'s subprocess-path finally cleanup removes the same pid-scoped file
- Unit tests in test/unit.test.mjs (Group 9, RLM Prompt Building) updated to assert the pid-scoped path appears in the agentic prompt
- node --test test/unit.test.mjs stays green

title: SDK mode unusable from installed hook location — document or fix dependency resolution
description:
install.sh copies only rlm-hook.mjs and rlm-hook.sh to ~/.claude/hooks/. The Phase 2 SDK path lazily imports @anthropic-ai/sdk (createAnthropicClient, rlm-hook.mjs approx line 939), but Node module resolution from ~/.claude/hooks/ will not find the SDK installed in the repo checkout's node_modules — so for a normally-installed hook, RLM_USE_SDK=true silently falls back to the subprocess path on every run (the import throws, the catch logs and degrades). Users following README get a feature that cannot activate. Also note plan.md Phase 2 said 'Add @anthropic-ai/sdk as optional dependency' but package.json lists it under dependencies.

Fix options (choose one):
a) install.sh additionally installs the SDK next to the hook (npm install --prefix ~/.claude/hooks @anthropic-ai/sdk) when the user opts into SDK mode,
b) resolve the SDK relative to the source repo (e.g. try import from a configurable RLM_SDK_PATH), or
c) document clearly in README that SDK mode requires running the hook from the repo checkout (point settings.json at the checkout path instead of ~/.claude/hooks/) and move the SDK to optionalDependencies per the plan.

Acceptance criteria: a user can enable RLM_USE_SDK=true following only the README and observe the SDK path being used (log line 'Used SDK-Direct ... path' in the rlm-hook log); package.json dependency classification matches the plan or the plan is amended; install.sh and README agree.

title: Semantic cache hygiene: clean up orphaned .embedding sidecars and stale index.json entries
description:
Plan Phase 3 (docs/plan/plan.md) explicitly lists 'Index needs compaction as cache grows' as a tradeoff, but no compaction was implemented. In rlm-hook.mjs, checkCache (approx line 131) deletes only the expired <key>.json cache entry; the companion <key>.embedding sidecar (written by saveCacheEmbedding, approx line 1416) and the key's inline vector in index.json (updateCacheIndex, approx line 1386) are never removed. Consequences: the cache dir grows without bound with orphaned float32 sidecars; semanticLookup (approx line 1533) keeps scoring stale vectors on every SHA miss (scoreFromIndex and scoreFromFiles both include them), paying I/O and cosine cost for entries that then resolve to 'entry gone' misses.

Fix (best-effort, gated like the rest of the semantic layer so failures never break the hook):
- when checkCache expires a <key>.json, also rm the sibling <key>.embedding (force) and drop the key from index.json
- and/or on 'semantic match but entry gone' in semanticLookup, delete that orphan embedding and prune the index entry so it never re-matches

Acceptance criteria: after a cache entry expires, its .embedding sidecar and index.json entry are removed on the next access path that discovers the expiry; a corrupt or missing index still degrades to the file scan; new unit tests in test/unit.test.mjs cover the orphan-cleanup path; existing groups 14-18 stay green.

title: Refresh README.md and CLAUDE.md to match shipped Phases 2-5
description:
README.md and CLAUDE.md document only the Phase 1 surface and have drifted from the code (rlm-hook.mjs). Concrete mismatches:

1. README Configuration section is missing all Phase 2-5 env vars defined in CONFIG (rlm-hook.mjs approx lines 32-76): RLM_USE_SDK, RLM_SDK_MAX_TOKENS (+ ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), RLM_SEMANTIC_CACHE, RLM_SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD, RLM_EMBED_MODEL, RLM_EMBED_BASE_URL (+ OPENAI_API_KEY), RLM_METRICS_FILE, RLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW, RLM_GATHER_CONTEXT.
2. README 'Example output' shows an XML-element structure (nested file elements etc.) that formatOutput (approx line 1601) never emits — the real output is pretty-printed JSON inside rlm_preresearch tags followed by a plain-text PRERESEARCH COMPLETE summary. Replace with a truthful example.
3. README Development section lists 'npm run lint' but package.json has no lint script — either add a lint script or drop the line.
4. README says nothing about the metrics dashboard (bench/dashboard.mjs --serve, port 9876) or Phase 4 context reuse; a short section for each would surface the shipped features.
5. CLAUDE.md documents an RLM_MODE env var (agentic|fast|detailed) that does not exist — the code uses RLM_AGENTIC_MODE and RLM_FAST_MODE. CLAUDE.md also says the hook is '664 lines, no external deps currently' (it is ~1880 lines with @anthropic-ai/sdk as a dependency) and frames Phase 2 as future ('Phase 2 adds the SDK').
6. README skip-detection table lists patterns (cargo build, bare question words) that only skip via the min-length rule, not dedicated patterns — align the table with shouldSkipRLM (approx line 159).

Acceptance criteria: every documented env var exists in CONFIG and vice versa; the example output matches what formatOutput actually prints; no references to nonexistent npm scripts or env vars; CLAUDE.md line counts and dependency claims accurate.

description:
